PrelimaryAudited_Summary2: Reported contact crimes increased, by 7,7% from                     608 059, in 2021/22, to 654 761, in 2022/23.
ReasonforDeviation_Summary:
Target not achieved.
The reported incidence of
contact crime may not be
a direct or reliable indicator
of police performance.
While it is important to track
crime rates, it is essential to
consider various factors that
can affect these statistics.
Crime rates are influenced by
a range of complex factors
and in particular violent or
contact crime, including
socio-economic conditions,
inequality, education levels,
drug abuse, community
dynamics and more.
Addressing these underlying
causes of crime requires long-term economic,
social and developmental
interventions that extend
beyond the scope of
immediate police responses.
Police responses primarily
focus on dealing with the
symptoms of the problem
by enforcing the law,
apprehending offenders and
maintaining public order. While
these efforts are necessary,
they are not sufficient to
address the root causes of
crime, comprehensively.
CorrectiveAction_Summary: The SAPS has developed a National Policing Strategy with the aim of creating an enabling environment for the allocation, management and deployment of resources, including human capacity, to fulfil its constitutional mandate of protecting and serving South Africans and their properties. To operationalise the implementation of the National Policing Strategy, the SAPS issued a National Crime Combatting Forum Instruction (NCCF) Instruction No. 18 of 2022. This instruction focuses specifically on Focus Area 4 of the strategy, which pertains to the prevention and investigation of crime that poses a threat to the well-being and safety of all people in South Africa. The NCCF Instruction outlines four implementation requirements, which are integrated and measured in the Department's Annual Operational Plan and Annual Performance Plan. These implementation requirements are as follows: the immediate stabilisation of the National Top 30 High Contact Crime Station, interventions at the Top 20 High Contact Crime Stations in each province, interventions by Head Office Generals at the Top 30 High Contact Crime Stations and the implementation of Provincial Violent Crime Reduction Plans.
ValidatedAudited_Summary2:
Reported contact
crimes increased,
by 7,7% from
608 059, in
2021/22, to
654 761, in
2022/23.
ReasonforDeviation_Q1: Contact crimes are frequently generated by, among other causes, the excessive consumption of liquor and drugs, gang-related violence, domestic violence and organised crime. It is clear that these causative factors range from social behaviour, criminal behaviour and group behaviour.  Most of the social behaviour offences occur in secluded or private social settings, while group behaviour happens in public areas, like streets. The majority of social behaviour offences are perpetrated by people who know each other, ranging from been known by sight/name, to an intimate partner or parent. As a result, the SAPS cannot easily address these crimes by conventional policing strategies. Liquor, substance abuse and environmental design factors also play a key role in the commission of these crimes.
CorrectiveAction_Q1: National Crime Combating Forum (NCCF) Instruction 1, Operation Vhuthu Hawe, which will run until 2025, aimed at introducing measures to increase police visibility and stabilise hotspot areas.                                                                                                        The development of the National Policing Strategy is in its final stages and has been developed to reaffirm the SAPS's determination to prevent, combat and investigate crime and to consciously reinforce the general public’s feeling of being safe and secure.

ReasonforDeviation_Summary:
During the 2022 AENE process, an amount of R6 billion was declared a saving on the SRD R350 grant
A 2nd Adjustment Budget was tabled in March 2023 where an additional amount of R3.7 billion was declared a saving on the SRD R350 grant, which resulted that a total amount of R9.7 billion was declared a saving on the SRD R350 grant for the 2022/23 financial year
CorrectiveAction_Summary:
During 2022/23 financial year, National Treasury imposed “imposed declared savings” on the SRD R350 grants to the amount of R9.7 billion, which reduced the annual allocation for social grants related to the 2022/23 financial year. 
This was because of the Department had introduced a stricter bank verification as a method to check the eligibility of all applicants. 
Since the income threshold was set at R350, the majority were found to have received income in excess of that threshold, and were therefore excluded. 
Although the Department decided to increase the means test threshold to R624, the number of beneficiaries did not increase sufficiently to exhaust the allocated budget and majority of beneficiaries were found to have received income exceeding the means test.
ReasonforDeviation_Q1: Payments was revised based on revised cashflow requirements in terms of SOCPEN data.
CorrectiveAction_Q1: SOCPEN data aligned to cashflow requirements
ReasonforDeviation_Q2: This was due to misalignment of SOCPEN data and cash flow requirements
CorrectiveAction_Q2: The SOCPEN data will be aligned to cashflow requirements action
ReasonforDeviation_Q3: This was due to misalignment of SOCPEN data and cash flow requirements
ReasonforDeviation_Q4: The deviation was a result of declared savings by NT on the SRD 350 grant of R5.3 b in the 2022 AENE and R3.7 b in Feb 2023
CorrectiveAction_Q4: As per an agreement between the Department, SASSA, and National Treasury
